'''''Equisetum'' × ''moorei''''' is a naturally occurring [[nothospecies]] of ''[[Equisetum]]'' native to Europe and Asia.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Equisetum × moorei Newman {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:92994-2 |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

The hybrid formula is ''[[Equisetum hyemale]]'' × ''[[Equisetum ramosissimum]]''.<ref name=":0" />

== Distribution ==
The native range of the hybrid is Western to Central Europe, including the Baltic States, Ireland, Iceland and South European Russia as the furthest point in Europe. Additionally, it is native to Asia, namely Japan. It has notably gone extinct in Sweden.<ref name=":0" />

== Habitat ==
Found in forests and damp, disturbed areas, such as clay banks and stream banks.<ref>Luxford,  George, & Newman,  Edward. (1841). ''The Phytologist: a popular botanical miscellany'' (Vol. 5, p. 19). John van Voorst. </ref>
